title: How to animate humans
author: saskinas
selftext:
Animating people has always intimidated me! Now that AI is around, I am hoping I can get through this roadblock, but as I’m trying to research what you all are trying, I still see very little human animation posted. I have been using Claude, and a text to animation pipeline might be what I need, could anyone tell me how it has worked out for them? I could also try to learn animation by hand, my worries about that being how much I can do solo. Part of me has this feeling that if I give it a month, someone is going to release a really good tool for this!

My use case right now is a procedurally generated world, mostly I just need to make all the people look busy! Hammering stirring etc.

comments.author: Right-Statement367
comments.body: I’m just curious, coz I have no idea how does it work. How do they know that someone uses their animations or whatever?

replies.author: AdHom
replies.body:
Honestly it's doubtful they would. Someone familiar enough with their specific motion captures to actually notice would have to play your game and care enough to take legal action. Even if you're lucky enough to actually sell more than handful of copies it's still very unlikely. 

But nonetheless, if you're going to go through the cost and effort to commercially publish a game, it's probably best to avoid infringing on IP and risking a takedown or a lawsuit over such a small element too.

comments.author: MonkeyMcBandwagon
comments.body: I have not tried it yet, but RGB Mocap looks promising for converting camera or video feed to skeletal animations in most common formats. It is free and open source, runs on local GPU.
